text:
maria: quick check — I'm seeing a p95 TTFT spike for model-realtime on prod after the rollout. Where's the single-pane view for TTFT + tokens/sec by model/version? need a pointer and any quick triage steps :eyes:
dan: grafana has a combined panel: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/latency/ttft-overview. filter for `env=prod` and `model=MODEL_NAME`. there's a dropdown for version. p95/p99 shown as lines, tokens/sec as the bar.

use the 'token-rate' panel for tokens/sec trends. if you want the promql: `sum(rate(tokens_emitted_total{env=\"prod\",model=\"MODEL_NAME\"}[1m])) by (model,version)` — that'll give you tokens/sec.
jess: logs + traces: app logs in Loki -> `{job=\"inference\",env=\"prod\",model=\"MODEL_NAME\"}`. for slow TTFT, filter spans in Jaeger with operation `serve.request` and tag `model:MODEL_NAME`. quick jaeger link: https://jaeger.redwood.company/search?service=inference&tags=model:MODEL_NAME

kevin: fwiw, p95 up doesn't always mean system CPU. check `kv-cache-hit_rate` and `batch_size` distribution on the same time window. small batches can tank tokens/sec and increase TTFT.

maria: thanks — dan, can you paste the exact dashboard panel names? I'm trying to add to my notes.
dan: panels: "TTFT: p50/p95/p99 (by model)" and "Token throughput (tokens/sec)". there's also a heatmap panel called "Batch size distribution" under the same dashboard. bookmark those.

jess: if you're triaging traces, look for long tail in `recv->response` span, then expand to `kv-cache` spans. sample jaeger trace id format: `3f2a1b...` — you can open a trace from the grafana table by clicking the trace id.

maria: any tips for alert tuning? current alert is firing on TTFT p95 > 800ms for 2m and we've been getting noisy alerts during traffic bursts.

kevin: for alerts, consider:
- raise to p95 > 1200ms for 5m as a stage, then tune from there;
- add `tokens/sec` as a correlate: only alert if p95 > threshold AND tokens/sec < baseline (means throughput drop),
- or use anomaly score: `increase(errors[5m]) / rate(requests[5m])` for real failures.

jess: +1 to adding tokens/sec signal. Loki alert idea: alert when `sum(rate(tokens_emitted_total[1m])) by (instance) < X` AND p95 TTFT > Y. that reduces noisy windowed spikes.

maria: great — i'll open a quick PR to adjust the rule and add a dashboard panel snapshot to the incident runbook. pinging reviewers: @dan @jess :eyes:. also i'm going to add a small sampling probe to force a KV cache warmup pattern to validate.

dan: reviewing, will do in ~30m. also add a note to check model-quantization variant fallback; sometimes fallback to fp16 causes perf shifts.

obs-bot: [ALERT] p95 TTFT exceeded 1.2s for model-realtime (prod) at 2812345650 — alert rule `ttft_p95_high`. auto-created incident: INC-2026.

maria: thanks obs-bot — linking incident to PR once available.

kevin: if you want a quick heatmap sample, run:```
curl -s "https://api.redwood.company/observability/heatmap?env=prod&model=MODEL_NAME&range=1h" | jq .
```that gives batch-size vs latency buckets.

jess: FYI i put a Loki quickquery snippet in the obs-runbook: `|~ "timeout|error|kv-miss" | json | count_over_time(1m)` — helps find correlated error spikes when TTFT climbs.

maria: perfect. i'll run the checks, open the PR, and post back results here. thanks all :thumbsup:

dan: lemme know if you want me to kick a canary traffic shift while you test — canary route: `canary/model-realtime/v2`

maria: will do. updating the incident with dashboards and plan.

kevin: one last note — for long-term, we should add a derived metric `tokens_per_ttft` (tokens/sec divided by p95) to make alerting simpler. filing a backlog ticket.

maria: awesome, filing the ticket now and tagging eng-ml.

jess: glhf — ping when PR's up and i'll review the Loki bits.

maria: PR: https://git.redwood.company/infra/observability/pulls/1423 — description: bump ttft alert window and add tokens/sec conjunctive condition + dashboard snapshot. reviewers: dan, jess.

dan: reviewing now.

kevin: thanks everyone.

maria: closing the loop: after the small canary and rule bump, alerts dropped and p95 returned to baseline. will keep monitoring 24h.

obs-bot: [RESOLVED] INC-2026 auto-closed at 2812345898 (alerts returned to normal).
